thread:
elaine_support: Customer escalation from ACME — user called the public API to issue a refund but our logs show the payments service invoked invoice.adjust instead. Customer hit it in prod twice. Full details below, need urgent triage.

james_support: Oof. Any error returned to the client or was the API 200 and the wrong side-effect happened?

elaine_support: API returned 200 with body {"status":"ok","id":"ref_123"} (client-facing). Internal audit log shows: routing.v1 -> payments.invoice.adjust invoked with args {"invoice_id":"inv_987","amount_adjustment":"-25.00"}. Customer expects refund.create with amount 25.00 and payment_method: card.

mike_eng_infra: Can you paste the original request payload (redact PII)? wondering if field names made the router fuzzy-match.

elaine_support: Here is the sanitized request we received from the customer:```json
{
  "customer_id": "cus_222",
  "invoice_id": "inv_987",
  "amount": "25.00",
  "direction": "negative",
  "note": "refund for duplicate charge"
}
```

sylvia_oncall: aha — router heuristics use both signature and payload features. "amount" + "invoice_id" + a negative "direction" could be interpreted as an invoice adjustment vs a refund. routing-bot should have chosen refund.create but apparently invoice.adjust had higher combined confidence for this payload. :eyes:

naveen_ml: I pulled the routing scores from the debug trie for that request id (logged at observability/requests/1767001123). Scores: refund.create -> 0.47, invoice.adjust -> 0.63. The model uses signature overlap + tokenized prompt features. The presence of invoice_id strongly boosts invoice.adjust.

mike_eng_infra: Can we reproduce locally? If we can craft the same input we can test a quick heuristic patch (penalize invoice.adjust when direction=negative and note contains refund).

elaine_support: Repro steps I used:
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.company/v1/support/action -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d @payload.json
2) watch logs: kubectl logs -f svc/routing -n prod | grep request:1767001123
3) observe: routing decision logged then downstream call to payments.invoice.adjust

naveen_ml: I ran a small experiment: adding a lightweight rule that increases refund.create score by +0.2 when note contains the token "refund" and direction is "negative" flips the choice. But that's brittle. We should instead retrain the reranker to include presence of payment_method and a flag for explicit refund intent.

james_support: Short-term: can we add a safeguard to the payments side to reject invoice.adjust when the payload includes payment_method or explicit refund language, and return a 409 / escalate? Customers seeing silent wrong side-effects is worse.

mike_eng_infra: Agreed. I'll open a canary fix: payments service will validate a whitelist for invoice.adjust (only allow when "adjustment_reason" present and direction != negative) and reject otherwise. Will push to staging, then a 5% canary in prod. CC @sylvia_oncall for rollout windows.

sylvia_oncall: OK for 5% canary for the next 30m window. If we see <0.1% client errors we rollback.

naveen_ml: For the mid-term plan: I'll create a dataset of these ambiguous examples from support logs, add a binary feature for explicit "refund" tokens and invoice_presence, and retrain the reranker. Will target a rollout in the next inference-model cycle (2 weeks).

elaine_support: Also adding this customer case to our support playbook with recommended client-side mitigation: include "intent": "refund" or include "payment_method" to avoid ambiguity. Will notify the customer that we're doing a canary and will follow up.

james_support: Thanks. Anything else we should capture now? Requesting eng postmortem if this affects >1 customer.

routing-bot: automated note: created ticket ROUTE-4821 (priority: high) tracking "ambiguous payload leads to invoice.adjust instead of refund.create". Linked logs: observability/requests/1767001123.

mike_eng_infra: I'll attach a quick repro script to the ticket and the staging canary ID after deploy. Putting a reaction :rocket: when the canary goes live.

elaine_support: Customer updated — they received the wrong credit adjustment but are okay to wait for a manual refund while we fix. Marking case escalated. Thanks everyone.
